https://www.theguardian.com/uk-news/2026.text: Insp Joel Brady with his family: ‘This is a massively positive step and great news for policing fathers.’ Photograph: Joel Brady View image in fullscreen Insp Joel Brady with his family: ‘This is a massively positive step and great news for policing fathers.’ Photograph: Joel Brady Police Paid police paternity leave to double after fathers reported being ‘ostracised’ Exclusive: Pay increases to two weeks in England and Wales after Guardian revealed officers ‘mocked’ for taking time off Alexandra Topping Political correspondent Wed 12 Aug 2026 02.00 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google Paid paternity leave for police in England and Wales is to double, after the Guardian revealed last year that officers were “mocked and ostracised ” for taking time off to spend with their babies. The home secretary, Shabana Mahmood, has increased the amount of paid parental and adoption leave for officers from one week to two across all forces, with fathers’ leave upped to be in line with mothers’. Before the change, only a quarter of forces offered two weeks’ full pay, with others offering one week on full pay and the second week on statutory pay. This resulted in only 40% of officers in the latter group taking the second week’s leave, compared with 88% of those in the first group. Civilian staff in the Metropolitan police were entitled to three weeks’ paternity leave at full pay. The policing minister Sarah Jones said: “Police officers work tirelessly to protect the public, so it is right that new fathers are better supported to spend time with their families. By expanding police paternity leave, we are recognising the importance of family life.” View image in fullscreen Before the change, only a quarter of forces offered new fathers two weeks’ paternity leave on full pay. Photograph: Paul Hennell/Alamy The government is now coming under increased pressure to improve paternity leave across the public sector, which campaigners argue offers poor and patchy leave for fathers. The win for police officers has galvanised a campaign for better paternity leave for military fathers, with the Conservative peer Joanna Penn tabling an amendment to the armed forces bill that would triple paternity leave to six weeks for serving personnel. The government-led tri-forces survey last year found that nearly 30% of families in the armed forces were separated for more than three months in the last year. A survey of 450 serving parents by the campaign group The Dad Shift found that more than 95% agreed the current paternity offer was not enough. “We ask so much of our military families,” said Penn. “The least we can do is give new fathers the chance to properly support their partners and bond with their babies.” Campaigners, backed by MPs on the women and equalities select committee , are pushing for a change to give fathers six weeks of paternity leave at 90% of pay. The UK’s statutory paternity leave of two weeks, paid at £184.03 a week, is one of the worst in Europe. Recent research found one in three UK fathers took no paternity leave after the birth of their child. An 18-month government review of the UK’s parental leave system is expected to report in December. Joel Brady, a police inspector who was part of the campaign, said the policy change would give thousands of fathers in the police more “precious time” with their babies. “This is a massively positive step and great news for policing fathers who want to be there for their partners and involved in their children’s lives,” he said. “I’m optimistic that the government will now listen to dads and increase the amount of leave available to all of us.” More than 20 organisations – including a new group of Labour MPs that has been lobbying ministers to improve rights for fathers – have written to Andy Burnham urging him to commit to the men and boys’ agenda, which gathered pace under Keir Starmer. In November, the government launched the first men’s health strategy for England , and Starmer assigned the then deputy prime minister, David Lammy, to lead work across the government to improve outcomes for men and boys. Writing to the new prime minister, the group said: “Taken together, these developments represent something more significant than a series of individual policies. They represent the beginning of a new consensus: one that rejects the false choice between supporting men and supporting women.” George Gabriel, a co-founder of The Dad Shift, said: “Times are changing. This is the most active generation of dads there’s ever been and momentum is clearly building across the public sector for better paternity leave. “If Andy Burnham wants to prove his is a cost of living government then, as their review of parental leave concludes later this year, we hope they’ll get alongside working families at one of the moments that matters the most.” Explore more on these topics Police Maternity & paternity rights Metropolitan police Parents and parenting Family Employee benefits Children news Share Reuse this content Most viewed Most viewed The Filter Wellness Fashion Food Recipes Love & sex Home & garden Health & fitness Family Travel Money

https://www.theguardian.com/australia-ne.text: Four people have been injured after a drive-by shooting in Loganholme, south of Brisbane, outside a venue hosting a boxing event. Photograph: Ben Smee/The Guardian View image in fullscreen Four people have been injured after a drive-by shooting in Loganholme, south of Brisbane, outside a venue hosting a boxing event. Photograph: Ben Smee/The Guardian Queensland ‘Horrific’: woman, 19, shot in head in drive-by shooting outside boxing event near Brisbane Offenders still at large after shots fired from vehicle outside licensed premises in Loganholme Get our breaking news email , free app or daily news podcast Australian Associated Press Sat 24 Oct 2026 21.41 EDT First published on Sat 24 Oct 2026 19.13 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google Four people have been injured after a drive-by shooting outside a venue hosting a boxing event, including a 19-year-old woman who was shot in the head. Queensland police Detective Inspector Ian Galpin said a group of people were gathered at the passenger drop-off zone outside Fitzy’s Loganholme, south of Brisbane, about 8.18pm on Saturday when a Mitsubishi pulled up. Galpin said police would allege a “number of shots” were fired from the front window of the pub where two males wearing balaclavas and gloves were sitting, striking four people. A Jimboomba woman, 19, was shot in the neck and head. She has undergone surgery and remains in a critical condition. Speaking on Sunday, Galpin described her as an “innocent bystander”. “It’s horrific. It’s something that her family should never have to go through.” Three others were injured and remained in serious but stable conditions: a Browns Plains man, 38, shot in the abdomen and arm, a Salisbury man, 37, shot in the abdomen, and a Cornubia man, 27, shot in the abdomen. Galpin alleged the Mitsubishi was set alight on Maloney Road at Waterford West, which was declared a crime scene, while a second car collected the occupants of the Mitsubishi and departed. “It is possible one of these persons from the Mitsubishi was injured or burnt during this process,” Galpin said. Sign up for the Breaking News Australia email Galpin said it was too soon to say whether it was related to organised crime. “This is a horrific event in a public space where adults and children were simply trying to enjoy a sporting event and this incident, it’s clearly not acceptable. We will not tolerate it.” Speaking on Sunday morning, Logan’s mayor, Jon Raven, described residents in the area as frightened. “This has sent a shock wave through Logan. We’ve never seen something like this in Logan before,” Raven told the Today show. “Our hearts go out obviously to the victims and the staff and the people at this boxing event. “I’ve been to one of these events before, they’re [a] really family friendly environment, and I know there’s lots of children who were there, and this will impact them for the rest of their lives.” The deputy commander of Queensland police, Chris Stream, described the scene as “confronting”. “A number of people had suffered gunshot wounds,” he told Today. View image in fullscreen Bullet holes visible in the wall at Fitzy’s Loganholme. Photograph: Ben Smee/The Guardian Raven said the event had been organised to help children steer clear of violence. “[The organiser] will be devastated this has happened because he loves boxing and uses it as a tool to empower and reconnect young people who might be going off the rails, and this is the opposite of what he’ll want to see,” Raven said. Logan City Titles shared a statement on social media on Sunday morning. “We are heartbroken about the incident that occurred at the fight night,” it read. “Logan City Titles was a family event, an event for our community, showcasing local talent, hard work and everyone’s skills inside the ring. “These types of incidents have no place in the boxing community or any part of the broader community.” The offenders were still at large on Sunday but police said they did not believe there was an ongoing threat to the public. Police were urging anyone with information to contact them.
